contributions.statement: Before asking an LLM to hunt for design gaps in a natural-language interface spec, have it extract the spec into an explicit state machine and search that; free-text prompting over the raw spec found nothing confirmed.
contributions.evidence: §V RQ1: 2 zero-shot Opus runs gave 9 candidates, all rejected; FSM-grounded runs gave 11 expert-kept findings. Baseline is two prompts judged by the authors' own C2 verifier; FSM accuracy shown only on a TCP proxy (Table I).
relative_to: P35 formal methods / spec formalization before analysis

contributions.statement: Do not adopt A2A delegation across trust boundaries without adding your own identity propagation and capability attestation; the spec itself leaves context ownership and capability claims unverifiable.
contributions.evidence: Table III, §VI: 11 spec-level issues (cross-client context injection, credential harvesting across hops, unattested capabilities); exploits reasoned over the FSM, not demonstrated on live implementations.
relative_to: authenticate peers and verify capability claims across trust boundaries (zero trust)

reason: The FSM-first idea is the only transferable heuristic and its baseline is a strawman judged by the authors' own verifier; the A2A findings matter only to teams adopting A2A and restate zero-trust practice.
